thread:
morgan: Quick report from onboarding dogfood: the new Next + LangChain starter hangs during the eval harness when using the JS streaming client. Python/LlamaIndex path completes fine. Repro + logs below.

devon: Yikes. Hanging how — request in-flight forever or error after timeout?

morgan: In-flight. Browser shows spinner, serverless lambda never returns. Local Node logs show the request enters the runtime, you see tokenization and first chunk output in stdout, then nothing. No error, connection stays open until CI timeout (~3m).

Logs from serverless function (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-20T14:12:03Z] incoming request /api/chat
[2026-03-20T14:12:03Z] redwood-js: streaming.start model=chat-lite-v2
[2026-03-20T14:12:03Z] token-stream: chunk 1 -> "Hello"
[2026-03-20T14:12:04Z] token-stream: chunk 2 -> " there"
# no more chunks, no close event
```

priya: Does the JS client send a final `DONE` or `event: done` like the Python one? Maybe our SSE framing is different.

morgan: I instrumented the outgoing wire and the JS client stops sending keep-alive pings after chunk 2. Python keeps the connection alive. Looks like the browser fetch stream is not flushed because the SDK's internal buffer waits for a newline terminator.

tiernan: We changed the JS stream flush to reduce CPU for small chunks last quarter; seems that optimization regressed serverless setups where V8 batching + platform buffering leads to no data egress until buffer fills.

devon: Repro steps (local):
1) clone repo `github.com/redwood/inference-samples/next-langchain-chat-starter`
2) `yarn && yarn dev`
3) open /chat, start convo with a long prompt that triggers streaming (system + user messages)
4) observe spinner > 2min; check function logs

ci-bot: CI run #3127: 2 failing onboarding checks (chat-starter stream-hang). Full trace: https://ci.internal/runs/3127 :eyes:

priya: Short-term mitigation: change starter to use non-streaming API for serverless demo (i.e., fetch full response) and add a warning in README about streaming caveats on Vercel/Netlify. Longer-term: revert the buffer batching change or add platform-aware flush heuristics.

tiernan: I can put up a small patch to the JS SDK: add `forceFlush: true` option for streaming calls, which will emit newline terminators and micro-flush after each chunk when enabled. We'll default it off but enable in starter dev config. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/inference-js/pull/456 (WIP).

morgan: That sounds perfect. Action items:
- tiernan -> finish PR to add `forceFlush` and unit test simulating serverless buffer (assign to you)
- devon -> update Next starter to opt-into `forceFlush` in dev/staging and change CI harness to test both streaming and non-streaming paths
- priya -> add README note and a short troubleshooting section for streaming hangs on managed serverless platforms

morgan: Also let's add a tiny playground script in the starter that toggles `forceFlush` so devs can see the diff quickly.

priya: Will do. Re-running the eval harness once the canary lands.

morgan: Thanks all, this one explains a lot of friction we've seen in #help where new users report "chat never finishes". Hope this patch fixes onboarding pain. :pray:
